Quick range changes can finish out of order.

terms.meaning: how closely the user followed their medicine schedule.
a shared place that holds app data, which screens read from and update.
a small library that provides such a store.

sections.name: File setup, PeriodKey
sections.title: Setup and time range options
sections.what: Brings in the store library and the API client, and defines the five time ranges: 7 days, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months and 1 year.
sections.why: Limits the range to the options the server supports.

sections.name: AdherenceData
sections.title: Medicine adherence data shape
sections.what: Describes the adherence data: a rate, counts of taken, skipped, missed and total doses, and a daily series.
sections.why: Gives the dashboard a clear shape to draw from.
sections.watch_out: The file does not say whether the rate is a percentage or a fraction.

sections.name: WaterData
sections.title: Water intake data shape
sections.what: Describes water intake: average, best, days the goal was hit out of days, and a daily series.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed shape for the water card.
sections.watch_out: The average and best values are text, so any math on them needs converting first.

sections.name: SleepData
sections.title: Sleep data shape
sections.what: Describes sleep: average, best and worst hours, and a daily series.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed shape for the sleep card.
sections.watch_out: The file does not say how hours are rounded.

sections.name: HealthTrend
sections.title: Lab trend data shape
sections.what: Describes one health measurement, such as a lab value: its name, value, unit, normal range, whether it is out of range, status, trend text and direction, and a short history for a small chart.
sections.why: Lets a lab result be shown with its trend.
sections.watch_out: The value is text, not a number, so comparing it with the range needs care.

sections.name: HealthScoreData
sections.title: Health score data shape
sections.what: Describes the overall health score and its three parts: adherence, lab results and activity. Each part has a weight and a value.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the score be explained part by part.
sections.watch_out: Nothing here checks that the weights add up to a fixed total, so a mismatch would skew the score without warning.

sections.name: AnalyticsState
sections.title: What the store holds
sections.what: Lists the dashboard data kept in the store, the chosen range, the loading flag, and two actions: change the range and reload.
sections.why: Keeps all dashboard data in one place.
sections.watch_out: Changing the range reloads everything, so each change makes a new server request.

sections.name: useAnalyticsStore
sections.title: Loading and reloading the dashboard
sections.what: Starts on a three-month range. Changing the range saves it and reloads. Reloading fetches the whole dashboard in one request and stores each part. If the request fails, loading turns off and the old data stays.
sections.why: Likely reason: one request keeps every card on the screen in step.
sections.watch_out: A failed reload keeps the old numbers on screen without any message, so they can look current when they are not.

summary: Holds the dashboard numbers for medicine adherence, water, sleep, lab trends and the health score, and reloads them when the time range changes.
purpose: Feeds the analytics view with current numbers for the chosen time range.
why: Likely reason: one request for the whole dashboard keeps all its parts in step.
how: Starts on a three-month range with no data. Changing the range saves it and reloads. Reloading asks the server for the dashboard, then stores each part. If the request fails, it turns off loading and logs the error.
inputs: The chosen time range and the dashboard response from the server.
outputs: Stored dashboard data and a loading flag.
risks: A failed reload keeps the old numbers with no message. Two quick range changes can finish out of order and show the older range. The code assumes a fixed response shape.
debug: If the dashboard is blank, look for the message 'Failed to fetch analytics' in the log and check the response shape. If numbers look out of date, the last reload probably failed.
